newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Utd News targets review by yr-end.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Utd News targets review by yr-end.

text.p: Newly-enlarged United News & Media plans to complete a review of its portfolio of businesses by the end of the year, chief executive Clive Hollick said in a telephone interview on Thursday.
"We're going to aim to have completed the review by the end of the year," Hollick told Reuters.
The review follows the merger completed in April between United News and MAI Plc.
Hollick said he thought United's interim performance was "at the top end of expectations" and that progress on integrating the two groups had been slightly more rapid than expected.
Pre-tax profit for the six months rose some 21 percent to 151.9 million stg.
"We have set a fairly fast pace," Hollick said, adding that the steps taken as part of the reorganisation should generate improved margins over the next decade.

Costs from the merger to date amount to 56.4 million stg. Of this 23.9 million stg covers property costs and the rest relates to redundancy, retraining and the write-off of assets. Hollick forecast a payback on these costs over the next three years.
Costs from the reorganisation of Express newspapers and the profit on the sale of Tolley will be taken in the second half.
The Express reorganisation is expected to cost 32 million stg and the Tolley sale should generate 82 million.
The Express titles are to switch to a seven-day operation in an attempt to stem their declining circulation.
"Our aim is to revitalise the Express. There has been too little investment over the years but we aim to improve the quality and range," Hollick said.
He stressed that the Express would be given time to close the gap on the mid-market leading Daily Mail.
"We are not looking for quick and easy answers. Investing a substantial amount of money is the way forward," he said.
